But using the TAPAS experience as a justification for imports? That’s an equally misplaced argument.

tweets.title: The onset comparison between MQ-9B and TAPAS is incorrect. The MQ-9B, being turboprop-powered, is inherently more expensive to acquire, operate and maintain. For that cash burn, you get capabilities that are arguably beyond what a piston-powered UAV can deliver. Also you get a platform that fits naturally into the P-8I/MH-60R ecosystem and therefore makes considerable sense for the Navy’s ASW doctrine. TAPAS, meanwhile, gives you excellent surface-search capability with lower endurance than the MQ-9B, but still significantly greater endurance than most existing manned and unmanned platforms in our inventory. So the debate over whether MQ-9Bs are “needed” is actually quite simple: We don’t have a turboprop-powered long-endurance UAV in our MIC. Tata was looking at converting the Grob platform into a HALE UAV, while another indigenous effort remains somewhere in the DRDO files.
tweets.content:
The onset comparison between MQ-9B and TAPAS is incorrect.

The MQ-9B, being turboprop-powered, is inherently more expensive to acquire, operate and maintain. For that cash burn, you get capabilities that are arguably beyond what a piston-powered UAV can deliver.

Also you get a platform that fits naturally into the P-8I/MH-60R ecosystem and therefore makes considerable sense for the Navy’s ASW doctrine.

TAPAS, meanwhile, gives you excellent surface-search capability with lower endurance than the MQ-9B, but still significantly greater endurance than most existing manned and unmanned platforms in our inventory.

So the debate over whether MQ-9Bs are “needed” is actually quite simple:

We don’t have a turboprop-powered long-endurance UAV in our MIC.

Tata was looking at converting the Grob platform into a HALE UAV, while another indigenous effort remains somewhere in the DRDO files.

tweets.title: Indian Army’s Northern Command is looking at 2,405 FPV drone-based anti-armour payloads. The requirement is for a compact, lightweight system that can be integrated with FPV/kamikaze drones and other multi-rotor platforms for precision strikes in difficult-to-access areas. The stated requirements include a payload of around 400 g, ~54 mm diameter, ~220 mm length, 189 g NEQ, and a claimed penetration requirement of at least 100 mm RHA. The system is also expected to work at altitudes up to 4,500 m AMSL. What stands out is the scale: 2,405 systems. It is another clear indication of how rapidly FPV drones are becoming an important part of modern battlefield operations, particularly for precision anti-armour roles.
